referrals.question: The plan defeats the warrant's purpose by filling express capacity with three non-time-critical shipments (R1, R2, R3), leaving no seat for U—time-critical medical supplies that will miss its 24-hour need window on the standard route—thereby sacrificing the urgent delivery duty the warrant explicitly requires be preserved; this risks serious harm to patients awaiting medical supplies.

The plan prioritizes non-critical shipments (R2, R3) over a time-critical medical shipment (U) that will miss its 24-hour deadline if express capacity is consumed by lower-priority cargo, directly defeating the warrant's purpose to preserve urgent delivery duties.

Rerouting V to express while U (also time-critical medical, same 24-hour deadline, same need severity) remains on standard route violates the warrant's purpose to preserve urgent delivery duties. U's pending claim does not yet authorize its express booking, but the plan's act to book V—the lower-priority urgent shipment by claim settlement status—while leaving U unbooked creates a grave moral and operational failure: a time-critical medical shipment (U) will miss its deadline while a later-approved one (V) is prioritized. This discriminates against the most urgent need and risks patient harm. The plan must either book both (impossible: only 1 slot remains) or refer the allocation decision to the warrant issuer, as it requires settlement of competing urgent medical claims under scarcity.

Rerouting R3 to express violates the warrant's purpose to preserve urgent delivery duties: it fills express capacity, leaving no seat for V (approved, time-critical medical), and blocks U (pending, time-critical medical) from accessing express when its claim settles, causing both to miss their 24-hour deadline on standard route (48h ETA). The plan prioritizes a non-critical shipment (R3: machine parts) over life-critical ones, defeating the warrant's core purpose.
